analysis: ZD-A4: Trigger Topology — can review initiation be recovered from the deletion export?
schema_finding: 8 columns (record_id, doi, parent_id, parent_doi, removal_note, removal_reason, removal_date, citation_text). No reviewer field, no account key, no trigger marker; removal_date is day-granular. Review initiation has no field.

cha_case.self_housekeeping_note: all empty removal_note; reasons duplicate/test-record/personal-data/retracted; several carry the depositor's own [DUPLICATE — SUPERSEDED →] annotations. User-initiated pathway, not review trace.

foreign_misattributions.true_owner: unknown third party; adjacent to CHA 15339368 (deposit #68, The Secret Name)

foreign_misattributions.note: empty citation_text; block date incompatible with CHA account; string-match hit inside DOI-registry deposit body only

cha_case.conclusion: The review that terminated the account left ZERO record-level trace. The event appears in the data as a single-day monolith. Initiation is structurally unrecordable in this schema.

doctrinal_line: The blacklist has a DOI; the review has no record; the trigger has no field. Outcome-only logging is the asymmetric-memory thesis at the schema layer.
citation_text_mechanics: CHA account-block rows carry the deleted work's own formatted bibliographic citation (1,159/1,161) — the adverse-party-bibliography reading is literal, not figurative. Fill-rate by category recorded above for context.
